note: The most rows one batch of the accountant's valuations may carry, one row per asset. A larger file is split by the person who imports it; the file is refused as a whole, never cut.
The largest bank statement file this server reads, in bytes. A larger file is refused whole before it is read, and nothing is imported.
The most movements one imported bank statement may hold. The app and import_bank_statement_v1 refuse a file with more, whole; split it by period at the bank.

How many days before a movement an invoice may have been issued to be suggested for it by its amount and payer alone, when the movement carries no reference. A suggestion is always confirmed by a person.
The most figures one report page may ask for in a single read. A page that needs more is split into several reads; the batch is refused whole, never cut.

How long one report read may compute before the figures it has not reached yet are answered as timed out, so a page shows what it has instead of waiting for the server to give up. Keep it below the server request timeout.

The largest saved report definition in this space, in bytes of its stored text. The platform never stores more than 65536; a definition holds questions, never figures, so this bounds names, titles and texts.
The most pages one saved report may hold in this space. The platform never stores more than 4; a report over the limit is refused when it is saved, never cut.
The most cards (figures, tables, texts) one saved report may hold over all its pages. The platform never stores more than 24; a report over the limit is refused when it is saved, never cut.
How many months a monthly evolution looks back over, the current one included: 13 is a year and the same month a year ago.
How many quarters a quarterly evolution looks back over, the current one included: 9 is two years and the same quarter two years ago.
How many years a yearly evolution looks back over, the current one included.
Guardrail: the longest lead, in days, of a subscription invoice before the month starts. The server clamps to the same value.
How many minutes before its start a booking can be checked in. A minute grid wider than this widens it to one grid step.
Minutes before a booking starts at which the check-in reminder is shown.
Guardrail: how many days ahead a device schedules check-in reminders. A device scheduling horizon, not a booking rule.
Guardrail: how many unanswered booking questions one device keeps. A local recovery list, not an owner choice.
Shortest stay booked on the spot, used when the usual window would cross the end of the day.
Length of the stay booked on the spot (badge or space code) when the workspace books by the minute.
Guardrail: the longest range one calendar request may ask for. A platform-owned bound on the query.

The address-lookup service (Photon API) that places a published workspace address on the discovery map. An https address on the public internet, without credentials, query or fragment. Empty or invalid: the address this app build was given, else this default.

The tile server the discovery map is drawn from, as a template with {z}, {x} and {y} (and optionally {s} for a subdomain). An https address on the public internet, without credentials or fragment. Empty or invalid: the template this app build was given, else this default. Changing the host asks each person again before the map loads.
How many days ahead the member directory shows the next booking of a member.
Days after issue before a first reminder is suggested and before an invoice falls due when the workspace stated no payment term.

Seconds a server waits for the answer to a signed backchannel message (identity status, membership fact, membership snapshot) before it sends the same message again. At least 30: one attempt times out after 10 seconds. Keep it below the assertion lifetime, or a message lapses before its retry.

Hours a server keeps the receipt of a signed backchannel message, and a personal home the tombstone of an ended membership, before the hourly cleanup removes them. Never shorter than the longest assertion lifetime plus twice the clock skew, so a replayed or late message still finds what refuses it.

Seconds of clock difference between the personal home and a workspace server that are still accepted: a status issued further in the future is refused, and an expired one is honoured no longer than this.

How long a workspace server may rely on one identity status the personal home signed, counted from when the home issued it. At most 900 seconds: a suspended account is refused new requests within this time plus the allowed clock skew. Tightening it never extends a status already issued.

Seconds between two reconciliations of the identity status a workspace server holds for its linked people, independent of the app. Keep it below the assertion lifetime, or statuses lapse to stale between two runs.
Guardrail: the longest period one capacity figure may cover. A platform-owned bound on the query.
Guardrail: months beyond the first that one finance figure may span (23 means 24 months in all). A platform-owned bound on the query.
Minutes an assistant-requested action waits for the person to confirm it. A confirmation keeps the expiry it was created with. May be shortened, never lengthened.
Days an operator notice that has been read is kept before it is purged. Only read notices are purged: an unread notice, a grant, a consent and the audit trail are never touched by this value.
Minutes a successful check of the MCP endpoint stays fresh enough to turn the interface on. May be shortened, never lengthened.
Guardrail: the longest window one assistant read may ask for. A platform-owned bound on the query, not a permission to scan more.
Minutes after sending in which the author may still correct a message. A workspace message reads its own workspace, a personal or group message the platform value.
Groups one person may create per hour. May be lowered, never raised.

How many conversations one inbox source returns per page: the personal home its personal conversations and groups, a workspace server its workspace conversations and inquiries. A bound on one read, not on what the inbox holds.
Seconds between two refreshes of the inbox and its unread badge. Lower values load the server more.

Seconds between two timeout sweeps of a workspace's pending requests by one device. A request whose deadline passed is shown as timed out at most this much later. 0 sweeps before every read of the inbox.
Message requests one person may send per day to people who did not allow them. May be lowered, never raised.
Seconds between two refreshes of an open conversation. Lower values load the server more.
How many workspaces, people or groups the personal home returns per page of the new-discussion directory. A bound on one read, not on who may be written to.
The longest text the new-discussion directory searches for; a longer one is refused, never cut. A query default, not a rule about names.
How many servers the personal space asks at once when it gathers a person's own records. A bound on the device's parallel reads, not on any server.
Seconds the personal space waits for one server's answer before it shows that server as unavailable and goes on with the others.
Guardrail: the longest period one read of a person's reservations may ask for. A platform-owned bound on the query, resolved by the server that answers.
How many of a person's reservations one server returns per page. The server that answers resolves it once per read, whatever workspaces the page spans.
Days the personal space shows by default when it lists a person's reservations, and the window a read without an end date covers. A query default, not a booking rule.
Minutes after its last heartbeat a person still counts as online. Keep it above the 2-minute heartbeat.

Minutes the app must have been out of sight (in the background, a hidden tab, a sleeping kiosk) before it re-reads everything it shows when it comes back. A focus change never re-reads; a lost live connection always does, whatever this value.

A payable of at least this amount, in whole currency units, is paid by someone other than the person who approved its bill; splitting it into small payments does not get round the limit. 0 switches the rule off.

A supplier bill below this amount, in whole currency units, may be approved by the person who drafted or sent it, if that person may approve expenses. 0 keeps the rule that another person approves every bill. Rejecting always takes another person.
The most supplier lookups one person may make per minute on this server. A lookup over the limit is answered as throttled, nothing is sent to the registry, and the person may retry a minute later.
Seconds the server waits for a company registry (VIES) to answer one supplier lookup before the lookup counts as timed out. The person keeps what they typed and may retry or go on by hand.
Days an export the app recorded still counts as recent evidence that recovery works. Older than this, recovery reads as unverified.

source: records location (#2378): ETA s.286, ITA s.230
note: The reference of the CRA authorisation that lets a Canadian business keep its records outside Canada. Empty means none is recorded; the app then says the records are kept outside Canada without one.

The country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) where this installation keeps its database and backups, as its operator declares it from the hosting contract: one of the countries the app knows, or empty. Empty means not declared: the app then states no location.

Years a US space keeps its records when its state asks for longer than the federal default of the retention rule. A longer period extends every kind of record; a shorter one changes nothing. 0 means the rule applies. Never legal advice: confirm the period of your state.
Failed badge PIN attempts within the lockout window before a badge is locked. May be tightened (fewer attempts), never loosened.
Minutes over which failed badge PIN attempts are counted, and for which a locked badge stays locked. May be lengthened, never shortened.
The fewest digits a new badge PIN may have. A PIN set earlier keeps working until its owner changes it. A short PIN falls to a guessing script in days, so 6 is the default.
Failed PIN attempts across all badges of one workspace within the badge lockout window. Reaching this ceiling pauses badge sign-in and alerts the owners. May be tightened, never loosened.
Days a personal invitation stays redeemable. An invitation keeps the expiry it was created with. May be shortened, never lengthened.
Days a valid VAT-number check stays recent enough to stand as evidence on a new invoice. A shorter value asks for a fresh check sooner; it is not proof that a transaction is valid.
